defects: (a) BACKTICKS IN A DOUBLE-QUOTED COMMIT MESSAGE. The commit of G-MODULE-HEADER (relay 04aa0df4) wrote two quoted forms with backticks inside a double-quoted bash string; bash ran each as a command (not found) and the message lost them. Nothing else ran; every later message is single-quoted.

(b) A MEASUREMENT BANK WHOSE FIRST READING OVERSTATED ITS DATA. The lv build bank's first write said every run reached the hold within its first sample, where Genus5's attempts ran 657 s and 247 s, and gave ZeroActingPartial the low of its stopped attempt for its completed one; both readings recomputed from the rows before the bank was committed (786fd70f).

(c) AN ARM THAT FIRST READ NOTHING. G-MODULE-HEADER's first narrowing of the proof-word attachment read 0 claims over 239 headers -- a vacuous pass; caught by printing the matcher's yield, widened to the forms the headers use (a list before "are proved", "Proves", a colon list, a code span kept whole) before the opening run was banked (8 claims read).

(d) AN ARM THAT FIRST MATCHED A DIFFERENT DECLARATION. G-AXIOM-CLAIM's first lookup matched a covered declaration to a banked print by its last component alone, and so read SpectralSilence.silence_principle against SIDESilencePrinciple.silence_principle, another kernel's; caught on the trial before the opening run, narrowed to the exact name or the one banked name ending with it.

(e) TWO PLANTED EXPECTATIONS WRITTEN WRONG. test_axiom_claim.py (4) expected one contradicting declaration where the planted file has two (sorryAx; Lean.ofReduceBool), and test_name_b649.py (4) expected no mention of the name on the unmarked pages, whose glossary block carries the new entry; each expectation corrected, the tools unchanged.

(f) PAGES RE-EMITTED BEFORE THE GLOSSARY THEY CARRY WAS COMPLETE. Component 5 re-emitted both pages (PLACE-papers 47e09ce, ac0603f) when the glossary held the positivity clause alone; Component 6 then appended "act" and "the constant 1" (relay 957b64ca), and every page marked `# glossary` carries the whole glossary, so both pages regenerated two lines longer than committed and the page arms would have failed at HEAD. Caught while writing the suite, by regenerating the pages in scratch (119188 against 118771 bytes; 100634 against 100217); both pages re-emitted again one per call, the diff by kind the glossary block alone (PLACE-papers 50afbea, d208568), the page arms and the frozen control 2 of 2 (relay data/b649_page_arms_c2.txt).

(g) A COMPOSER EDIT THAT SAYS ITS PHRASE TWICE. compose_v5's edit (f2) kept v4's phrase (its anchor F_ONE, "witnessed in the kernel at the constant 1 (trivialSummandPremise'_witness)") and set the glossary's entry for "the constant 1" after it; the entry opens "the value at which the restated premise is witnessed", so v5's dedekind_rhs' row reads "witnessed in the kernel at the constant 1, the value at which the restated premise is witnessed"; test_composer_b649.py (f2) checked the row against the same construction and did not read it for a repeated phrase. Caught by the sixth reader, its first UNCLEAR item (relay data/b649_desc_residue.txt (1)); not repaired in this act -- v5 is the act's description as composed, and the residue carries the row to the author's order.
short: (a) backticks in a double-quoted commit message
(b) a measurement bank whose first reading overstated its data
(c) an arm that first read nothing
(d) an arm that first matched a different declaration
(f) pages re-emitted before the glossary they carry was complete
(g) a composer edit that says its phrase twice
